newsitem.title: INDIA: India call rates crash, security prices rally.
newsitem.headline: India call rates crash, security prices rally.

text.p: Indian call money rates crashed on Monday to close at 1.00-1.50 percent on Monday, against the day's opening levels of 3.75-4.00 percent, dealers said.
"The market was quite easy today...no borrowers," a dealer at a state-run bank said. "Rates opened above three percent but poor demand and good liquidity pushed them down," he said.
Dealers said they expected call money to open around one percent on Tuesday.
Trade in government securities picked up on Monday with volumes rising to 4.27 billion rupees from the weekend's 3.57 billion rupees, dealers said
The 13.50 percent 1997 stock rose five basis points to 102.77 rupees, dealers said.

The zero-coupon bond maturing in 2000 was in demand on Monday with traded volume of 750 million rupees. It was traded between 63.62 and 63.70 rupees, compared to its last traded price of 63.53 rupees, dealers said.
Yields on treasury bills fell marginally, with October treasury bills shedding 20 basis point to 9.59 percent, dealers said.
The 91-day treasury bill auctioned last Friday at 8.20 percent was traded on Monday at 8.07 percent, they said.
